Liam — thanks, and excited to work with Peregrine. High level answers below and I attached a short MAP + network diagram to kick off the procurement discussion.

Quick checklist (cluster-level controls) — mandatory for our supported private deployment:
- KMS integration: customer keywrap via KMIP or cloud KMS (bring-your-own-key).
- PV encryption at rest (LUKS or CSI-side encryption) + encrypted backups.
- Audit export: kube-audit + application-level logs forwarded to your SIEM via TLS (we provide Kafka/HTTPS connectors).
- Private control plane: management plane traffic restricted to VPC/VLAN and mutually authenticated mTLS between control plane and worker agents.

Sizing sketch for a small pilot (conservative):
- Control plane: 3 nodes (m5.xlarge or equivalent VMs) for HA control plane components if you're virtualized; physical: 3 small rack servers.
- Inference pool (gpu): 2 nodes with 48–80GB VRAM equivalent (we usually recommend one gpus per replica for latency SLOs); if you use multi-instance GPUs we can tune.
- Worker pool (cpu): 2–3 nodes for batching, API frontends, sidecars.
- Disk: for model artifacts, a network-attached encrypted blockstore (minimum 1–2TB), local NVMe 1–2TB per GPU node for shardable KV cache and temp artifacts.

Network / egress patterns:
- No outbound public S3 access required: models can be pushed from your provisioning network to internal object store (S3-compatible) or via signed transfer over a bastion.
- We recommend an isolated egress gateway (single NAT/Bastion) with allowlist rules for control-plane updates (specific Redwood update URLs) and an allowlist for telemetry endpoints.

I've attached: Peregrine_MAP_v1.pdf (mutual action plan) and network-diagram-v2.png.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal technical kickoff with your ops team + 30–45 minute architecture readout (we can do next Wed).
2) You share hardware inventory and any compliance artifacts (SOC/Security questionnaire) to ops-infra@redwood.com.
3) We produce a deploy runbook and BOM template.

Stephanie — thanks for the context. High-level technical plan below (this is written for inclusion in the MAP + runbook):

1) Cluster topology (pilot, single-site HA):
- Control plane: 3 x m/medium VMs (or equivalently sized baremetal) behind private mgmt VLAN; etcd on isolated disks with regular snapshots to your internal objectstore.
- Nodepool gpu-inference (taints: dedicated=inference:NoSchedule): 2 x nodes (NVIDIA A10/A30 class or 2x smaller GPUs depending on budget), each with 1–2TB NVMe local for KV cache and temp store. Use RAID0 for performance but rely on replication at the application layer.
- Nodepool cpu-frontends: 2–3 x nodes for API, batching, sidecars.
- Optional burst pool (spot-preemptible) for large async jobs; controlled by autoscaler and RBAC.

2) Storage classes & policy:
- model-artifacts (encrypted-blockstore-csi): network-attached, CSI driver, encrypted at rest (KMIP or KMS). ReclaimPolicy: Retain for model artifacts.
- local-kv (local-ssd-csi): ephemeral local NVMe PVs for KV cache; mount as ReadWriteOnce and enable lifecycle hooks to pre-warm cache. ReclaimPolicy: Delete.
- backup-store: daily snapshot jobs to your internal S3-compatible endpoint via signed transfer; snapshots encrypted with customer key.

3) Encryption & key management:
- Customer KMS integration required. For LUKS on node-local volumes, use node-init scripts to unlock with KMIP agent at boot; store keys in HSM or your KMS.
- TLS between control plane and workers; mTLS with mutual cert rotation managed by our agent (we exchange certs via the provisioning shuttle).

4) Network/gating & egress controls:
- Deploy a single egress gateway (allowed egress) with strict ACLs. All outbound update checks and telemetry go through this gateway.
- Use VRF or VLAN segmentation for management vs. tenant traffic. Control-plane endpoints should be reachable only from management VLAN.
- For artifact transfers, use an internal objectstore with signed, short-lived URLs over HTTPS initiated from a jump-host (bastion) in the management network.

5) Observability & audit:
- Kube-audit shipped to your Splunk endpoint over TLS (customer certs).
- Node-level metrics via Prometheus pushgateway if network constraints require it; otherwise pull model.
- Add a lightweight agent to collect per-request latency traces to S3 (encrypted) and forward summary telemetry through the egress gateway.

6) Upgrade & rollout plan (pilot -> scale):
- Canary rollout for model-serving agent and runtime (10% of traffic to canary pool).
- Weekly maintenance window for platform upgrades; 48-hour rollback snapshot retained for artifacts.

Attachments for MAP: onprem-runbook-draft.md (one-page nodepool + storage spec), single-slide-network-gating.pdf (diagram stub).

- Confirm exact GPU model and whether passthrough/virtualization will be used.

- SLA target for latency and any regional compliance controls that exceed SOC2 baseline.
